statement: >= 90% of training compute of the 10 largest known 2027 training runs belongs to organisations headquartered in the two leading jurisdictions (Epoch AI notable/large-scale models database; snapshot 2028-03-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable in 2023 (resolves on 2027 runs). Context: 2023 analysis showed compute-intensive training runs dominated by Bloc A firms, with Bloc B labs lagging on every metric; the largest public estimate was ~2e25 FLOP for a Bloc A model.

items.summary: A Bloc A frontier developer released the technical report for its new flagship model, estimated in 2023 by the compute tracker as the largest known training run of the time (~2e25 FLOP).
items.detail: OpenAI, 'GPT-4 Technical Report', arXiv 2303.08774, 2023-03-15 (arXiv page verified via web_extract this run; the ~2e25 FLOP estimate is Epoch AI's, from item 002).

items.summary: Compute tracker analysis of industry AI research 2012-2023: leading Bloc A companies scaled training compute ~1e6-1e7-fold, far above the field's trend; Bloc B industry labs lag their Bloc A counterparts on all metrics, including compute-intensive runs.
items.detail: Epoch AI, 'Who is leading in AI? An analysis of industry AI research' (paper arXiv 2312.00043; verified via web_extract this run). Names Google, OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic vs Tencent, Baidu, Huawei; GPT-4 ~2e25 FLOP. Publication day approximated from the arXiv identifier (Dec 2023 listing).
items.value: GPT-4 ~2e25 FLOP; Bloc A firms lead all metrics

items.summary: A second Bloc A developer launched what it called its largest and most capable model family (three sizes), adding another frontier-scale run headquartered in Bloc A.
items.detail: Google, 'Introducing Gemini: our largest and most capable AI model', 2023-12-06 (verified via web_extract this run). Compute not disclosed in the post.
